title: Monthly Treasury Statement (Nov 2026 data) — the monthly deficit print
source: TSY: fiscaldata.treasury.gov — the November 2025 MTS (MonthlyTreasuryStatement_202511.pdf, p.40) was downloaded direct (HTTP 200, 3,622,616 bytes) and text-extracted with `pypdf` BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed session on 2026-09-08. Its Scheduled Release table reads verbatim 'Listed below are the scheduled release dates for the Monthly Treasury Statement. The Statement is released at 2:00 p.m.' with the accounting-month row 'November 2026 / December 10, 2026'. Corroborated twice, independently, in the same session: (1) the 8th-federal-workday rule this calendar validated 20-of-20 against Treasury's published 2024 and 2026 schedules computes December 2026's 8th federal workday as Dec 10 exactly (Dec 1 is a Tuesday, no federal holiday falls before the 10th); (2) Treasury's own services/calendar/release endpoint, fetched direct (HTTP 200, 965 rows), carries dataset 015-BFS-2014Q1-13 with exactly three forward releases — 2026-09-11, 2026-11-12 and 2026-12-10 — matching the published table row for row INCLUDING its September gap, at timestamps decoding to 14:00 ET on both sides of the DST boundary (18:00 UTC on 09-11, 19:00 UTC on 11-12 and 12-10). PROMOTED estimate -> confirmed by this session: the original estimate grounds were the lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep (the mts-august-2026-09-11 sweep found it), and re-fetching the primary in this event's own owning session clears them — the identical promotion mts-october-2026-11-12 made on 2026-09-05 from this same PDF. notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-08) after reading its one proposal, `from-mts-august-2026-09-11`, which is now shadowed. Two of the proposal's three framings hold and one is corrected. HOLDS: 2026-12-10 collides with cpi-2026-12-10 at 08:30 ET (same reference month — November 2026 — on both prints), and this is the densest corridor any MTS in this calendar has faced: 19 tracked events sit within +/-5 days against 6 for mts-october-2026-11-12, including fomc-2026-12-09 with its SEP and dot plot the prior afternoon. CORRECTED: the proposal says a funding lapse 'would hit this release's schedule before any other MTS in the window'. It cannot. The CR funds through 2026-12-11, so this 2026-12-10 release lands one day INSIDE the funded window, and November 2026's data is entirely within it too — lapse-clean on both counts. The exposed edition is the December-data statement the same Treasury table dates 2027-01-13. Nor do FT-50/FT-51 score here; they score 2026-09-11 and 2026-11-12 respectively and belong to mts-august-2026-09-11. THE FISCAL FINDING that earns this entry its own research: November 2026 and November 2025 both carry ZERO of the first-of-month military/VA/SSI/Medicare-drug benefit batches (Nov 1 is a Sunday in 2026 and was a Saturday in 2025, so each year's own batch pays out in the prior October; Dec 1 is a Tuesday in 2026 and was a Monday in 2025, so neither year pulls the next month's batch back). That makes this the SECOND consecutive calendar-clean y/y MTS comparison after October's, and the first clean at zero-vs-zero.
